decisions.executionNote: Approach the left gray nut with an open gripper, using a slowed elbow-up arc. Nut position is estimated from calibrated RGB; final alignment will use the wrist view.
Complete the slow overhead approach to the gray nut, then descend toward pickup height while keeping the elbow-up branch.
Correct the gray nut alignment leftward and forward from wrist RGB, close at pickup height, and make a small test lift to check retention.
Gray nut remains between the fingers after lifting. Carry it above the matching left gray bolt, keeping it upright and closed, then approach the insertion height.
Use the wrist view to center the gray nut laterally over the bolt, lower gently to engagement height, and begin a small clockwise tightening turn.
Continue a controlled clockwise gray-nut turn with a small axial descent. Keep the nut gripped and stay within the current wrist range; engagement is still being checked visually.
Open the left gripper and reset its yaw without lifting, preparing another tightening stroke while checking that the gray nut stays seated on the bolt.
The released gray nut appears tilted rather than securely threaded. Regrasp and lift slightly to inspect its orientation before attempting further insertion.
The gray nut now appears upright on its bolt after the lift. Descend open and regrasp it for an additional tightening stroke, without lateral displacement.
Tighten the upright gray nut clockwise through a limited wrist stroke with a one-millimeter axial descent, maintaining a closed grasp.
Reset the open left wrist for another clockwise gray-nut stroke, then reclose at the same height. The nut and bolt remain visually coaxial.
Allow the gray grasp to settle, then turn clockwise another two radians with only a one-millimeter axial feed. Keep the nut upright and the gripper closed.
Release and clear the gray pair, then move the left hand above the purple nut. Begin a slow elbow-up approach of the right hand toward the blue nut; both remain in their own workspaces.
Descend the left gripper toward the purple nut. Complete the right overhead rotation while adjusting its approach to the blue nut's observed location; keep both grippers open for visual alignment.
Refine the pickup alignment from both wrist views with small lateral corrections and a slow descent. The purple nut is visibly off-center, so keep both grippers open until alignment is checked.
Center the purple and blue nuts between their respective fingertips, close both grippers, and lift gently to verify that each nut is retained.
Carry the retained purple and blue nuts toward two separated central staging spots for table-mediated handover. Maintain height, closed grippers, and noncrossing arm paths.
Lower both nuts onto separated central table locations and open the grippers for a table-mediated exchange. Keep the hands on their respective sides of the centerline.
Withdraw both open hands upward and outward, then exchange their fore-aft approach lanes while preserving lateral separation. The left will collect blue and the right purple from the table.
Approach the staged blue nut with the left hand and purple nut with the right, staying just on each arm's side of the centerline. Descend open for wrist-camera alignment before grasping.
Lower the open grippers to the staged nut pickup height, close, and make a gentle test lift. Lateral alignment is imperfect, so retention must be checked from both wrist views.
Both nuts are visibly retained after the exchange. Lift for clearance and carry blue over the left blue bolt and purple over the right purple bolt, maintaining upright closed grasps.
Make small wrist-view centering corrections and lower both retained nuts toward their matching bolt tips. Pause near engagement height to inspect alignment before tightening.
Both nut openings now appear centered over their bolt tips. Lower gently to engage, then apply a clockwise tightening stroke with a small axial feed and closed grippers.
Release both nuts at their engagement heights and reset the open wrists for another clockwise stroke. Check that the nuts remain upright and aligned after release.
Both nuts stayed on their bolts after release. Lower slightly to regrasp the seated nuts, then apply another short clockwise tightening stroke with minimal axial feed.
The blue bolt top appears nearly flush with its nut, so release and clear that pair. Continue a small clockwise purple-nut stroke, then open and begin resetting the right wrist.

Withdraw the open left hand toward its home lane while preserving clearance. Reset and regrasp the purple nut with the right hand for another tightening stroke; blue and gray remain upright on their bolts.
Continue the right clockwise purple-nut stroke with a small axial feed. Gradually retract and unrotate the open left hand toward home, keeping elbow-up continuity and clearance.
Finish returning the open left hand toward its origin. Release the purple nut and reset the right wrist for another tightening stroke; its bolt top is still recessed compared with the other pairs.
Regrasp the still-seated purple nut and turn clockwise another two radians with a small axial feed. Keep the left hand open at its home position.
Release and reset the right wrist while keeping the purple nut seated. Its tip remains recessed, so prepare another limited tightening stroke rather than lifting the assembly.
Regrasp the purple nut and add a controlled two-radian clockwise stroke with two millimeters of axial feed. The other hand remains open at home; inspect the purple seating afterward.
Release the purple nut and withdraw vertically while resetting the open wrist. Inspect the unloaded pair, then return the right arm home if it remains upright.
The released purple pair remains upright with the bolt top near the nut face. Retract the open right arm toward home in a slow elevated arc; keep the left arm home and open.
Finish the right arm's slow return to its origin and make tiny left-home corrections. Leave both grippers open and the three upright matching assemblies undisturbed.
